source_text: וּ/בְנֵ֣י קֵינִי֩ חֹתֵ֨ן מֹשֶׁ֜ה עָל֨וּ מֵ/עִ֤יר הַ/תְּמָרִים֙ אֶת בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה מִדְבַּ֣ר יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּ/נֶ֣גֶב עֲרָ֑ד וַ/יֵּ֖לֶךְ וַ/יֵּ֥שֶׁב אֶת הָ/עָֽם־־׃
english_snapshot: And the descendants of the Kenite[a], Moses’ father-in-law, went up from the City of Palms with the descendants of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the Negev of Arad[d][c][b]; then he went and settled with the people.

signals.text: The Hebrew shifts to singular: 'then he went and settled.' This may refer to the Kenite clan as a collective singular, though some interpreters understand a plural sense.

source_text: וַ/יִּקְבְּר֤וּ אוֹת/וֹ֙ בִּ/גְב֣וּל נַחֲלָת֔/וֹ בְּ/תִמְנַת חֶ֖רֶס בְּ/הַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם מִ/צְּפ֖וֹן לְ/הַר גָּֽעַשׁ־־׃
english_snapshot: And they buried him within the territory of his inheritance[a], in Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

signals.text: Joshua 24:30 reads 'Timnath-serah' instead of 'Timnath-heres.' The difference is preserved here as a place-name variation in parallel burial notices.

source_text: וַ/תֵּ֣רֶא דְלִילָ֗ה כִּֽי הִגִּ֣יד לָ/הּ֮ אֶת כָּל לִבּ/וֹ֒ וַ/תִּשְׁלַ֡ח וַ/תִּקְרָא֩ לְ/סַרְנֵ֨י פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים לֵ/אמֹר֙ עֲל֣וּ הַ/פַּ֔עַם כִּֽי הִגִּ֥יד ל/ה אֶת כָּל לִבּ֑/וֹ וְ/עָל֤וּ אֵלֶ֨י/הָ֙ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַ/יַּעֲל֥וּ הַ/כֶּ֖סֶף בְּ/יָדָֽ/ם־־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: When Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart[a], she sent and called for the Philistine rulers, saying, “Come up this time[c][b], for he has told her all his heart.” Then the Philistine rulers came up to her and brought the silver in their hands.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'for he has told her all his heart.' In direct speech, some readers may expect 'me' instead of 'her,' but the received Hebrew text reads third person feminine singular.

source_text: וַ/יָּקִ֧ימוּ לָ/הֶ֛ם בְּנֵי דָ֖ן אֶת הַ/פָּ֑סֶל וִ֠/יהוֹנָתָן בֶּן גֵּרְשֹׁ֨ם בֶּן מְ ה֣וּא וּ/בָנָ֗י/ו הָי֤וּ כֹהֲנִים֙ לְ/שֵׁ֣בֶט הַ/דָּנִ֔י עַד י֖וֹם גְּל֥וֹת הָ/אָֽרֶץ־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then the sons of Dan set up for themselves the carved image, and Jonathan the son of Gershom, son of Moses,[a] he and his sons were priests for the tribe of the Danites until the day of the exile of the land.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'Moses'; the Masoretic tradition includes a suspended letter, yielding the traditional reading 'Manasseh.'

source_text: וַ/יָּ֨קָם אִישָׁ֜/הּ וַ/יֵּ֣לֶךְ אַחֲרֶ֗י/הָ לְ/דַבֵּ֤ר עַל לִבָּ/הּ֙ ל/השיב/ו וְ/נַעֲר֥/וֹ עִמּ֖/וֹ וְ/צֶ֣מֶד חֲמֹרִ֑ים וַ/תְּבִיאֵ֨/הוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔י/הָ וַ/יִּרְאֵ֨/הוּ֙ אֲבִ֣י הַֽ/נַּעֲרָ֔ה וַ/יִּשְׂמַ֖ח לִ/קְרָאתֽ/וֹ־׃
english_snapshot: Then her husband arose and went after her to speak to her heart and bring her back[a]. His young servant was with him, along with a pair of donkeys. She brought him into her father’s house, and when the young woman’s father saw him[b], he rejoiced to meet him.

signals.text: The Hebrew form in 'to bring ... back' is textually difficult; context indicates that he intended to bring the woman back.
